name: Greywalk Flatboot
description: A flat-soled ankle boot in grey synth-leather so cheap it creases white at every flex point. The seams are factory-done but barely — threads already pulling at the toe box on a new pair. Popular because they're one of the cheapest new-manufactured boots available, sold in bulk at Shelf market stalls. Most people buy two pairs at once knowing one will fail within months.
what_it_says: You're not pretending. These are what you could afford, and you're not making excuses.
worn_by: people just arriving in the city
story_hooks: Greywalk is a front company. Someone's tracking purchase data from every stall that sells them.
A pair still has the original sales tag — purchased the same day a person disappeared.
related_entities: Ringo Corponation SlipThread MX-3 Urban Cable Micro-Mobility Rig

physical_description.visual_profile: Utilitarian ankle boot with a blunt, squared-off toe and minimal design language. Sits just above the ankle with a rigid shaft. The silhouette is intentionally unremarkable—a functional base layer of street fashion rather than a statement piece. Looks worn and creased even when brand new.
physical_description.fit: Straight-cut, slightly boxy through the foot and shaft. No contour or tailoring. Designed for quick manufacturing rather than ergonomic fit. Comfortable enough for 8-hour shifts but not broken in naturally—wearers adjust to the boot rather than vice versa.
physical_description.primary_material: Cheap synth-leather composite, likely recycled polymer base with a thin PU coating. Splits easily along stress lines.
physical_description.texture: Slick and uniform out of the box with a plastic sheen. Creases develop immediately at the ball of the foot and heel—white stress marks become visible within days of wear, creating an aged, haggard appearance.
physical_description.color_scheme: Industrial grey with natural white creasing that develops organically. No dye variation or intentional weathering—the boot ages itself through use.
physical_description.closures: Side zip running from toe box to mid-calf. Zipper pull is basic stamped metal, often catches or jams by month two.
distinctive_features: Visibly loose seams at toe box and heel counter
Factory threading that appears already pulling on new pairs
Flat rubber sole with minimal tread pattern
Creases white at flex points within first week
Side zip prone to failure under stress
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5. The boot of the working precariat and unregistered. Affordable enough for bulk purchase but cheap enough that failure is built-in.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by warehouse workers, delivery couriers, street-level service jobs, and anyone without corp benefits or access to tier-locked retail. Buying two pairs simultaneously signals acceptance of disposability as economic reality. Common in the GLMZ's labor-surplus districts.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine pairs look already distressed due to material choice. After 3-4 weeks: seams separating at toe, creasing permanent and exaggerated, zip sticking. After 3 months: typically one boot is non-functional. Wearers often patch with friction tape or cheap adhesive rather than replace.
